hypotheses.reasoning: Origin is a long-open transaction on notif-db: at 12:41:09 notif-db reports TRANSACTION 93036 ACTIVE 82 sec held by template-svc-reconciler, holding a row lock on the notifications table (#1141). It's idle-ish (1 undo entry) and never commits, so every UPDATE notifications from template-svc waits. Downstream: notif-db 'Lock wait timeout exceeded' on UPDATE notifications (#1237, #1255); template-svc UPDATE cancelled by statement_timeout (#1267, #1310); notification-svc /render calls time out after 15s (#1270, #1314) and its template-svc connection pool saturates (#1340). Those then cause the api-gateway 504s (#1362, #1503, #1607, #1795), which are symptoms only. metrics-agent queue drops, billing-reconciler, redis and notif-worker are not implicated. Before the lock, the template-svc render path was healthy (~50-90ms, e.g. #1130, #1136), and no deploy or config change appears in the logs. The reconciler is the lock holder, but I could not find its start or the statement that left the transaction open, so the mechanism (a hung or uncommitted reconciler transaction) is inferred. It is classed as a hung query stuck behind a lock.

The template-svc connection pool exhaustion and retries amplify the lock stall into a gateway-wide 504 storm. However, the trigger is the lock holder, so this is a secondary classification of the same incident rather than the origin.

verdict.recommendedAction: Kill the stuck notif-db transaction 93036 held by template-svc-reconciler (or restart that reconciler job) to release the notifications row lock, then verify that UPDATE lock waits clear and POST /v1/notify latency and 504s recover. Follow up by adding idle-in-transaction and lock-wait timeouts, committing the reconciler in small batches, and checking why it held a transaction open for over 80 seconds.

hypotheses.reasoning: Origin is a long-open transaction on notif-db: at 12:41:09 notif-db reports TRANSACTION 93036 ACTIVE 82 sec held by template-svc-reconciler, holding a row lock on the notifications table (#1141). It's idle-ish (1 undo entry) and never commits, so every UPDATE notifications from template-svc waits. Downstream: notif-db 'Lock wait timeout exceeded' on UPDATE notifications (#1237, #1255); template-svc UPDATE cancelled by statement_timeout (#1267, #1310); notification-svc /render calls time out after 15s (#1270, #1314) and its template-svc connection pool saturates (#1340). Those then cause the api-gateway 504s (#1362, #1503, #1607, #1795), which are symptoms only. metrics-agent queue drops, billing-reconciler, redis and notif-worker are not implicated. Before the lock, the template-svc render path was healthy (~50-90ms, e.g. #1130, #1136), and no deploy or config change appears in the logs. The reconciler is the lock holder, but I could not find its start or the statement that left the transaction open, so the mechanism (a hung or uncommitted reconciler transaction) is inferred. It is classed as a hung query stuck behind a lock.
hypotheses.recommendedAction: Immediately kill the stuck transaction 93036 (template-svc-reconciler) on notif-db, or restart the template-svc reconciler job so it commits or rolls back. Then confirm the notifications lock waits clear and the render latency and gateway 504s recover. Afterwards, add a lock-wait / idle-in-transaction timeout and make the reconciler commit in short batches. Investigate why it held a transaction open for over 80 seconds.
